then.log: Low ulnar sensory and motor amplitudes but no slowing or conduction block across the elbow: not a focal ulnar neuropathy at the elbow.
The right medial antebrachial cutaneous sensory response is absent; the left is normal. The lesion is in the lower trunk or medial cord of the plexus, past the root ganglion.
Fibrillations in C8-T1 muscles supplied by both the ulnar and median nerves; cervical paraspinals normal.
Right ptosis and a smaller right pupil: a Horner syndrome.

why.question: Is this an ulnar neuropathy? What do the SNAPs tell you?

parts.label: What and why
parts.criteria: No. SNAP amplitude counts sensory axons distal to the dorsal root ganglion, so low ulnar and medial antebrachial cutaneous SNAPs put the lesion in the plexus, not the root; CMAP reflects motor axons, muscle and junction together; C8-T1 denervation across ulnar and median muscles with normal paraspinals fits a lower trunk plexopathy.
parts.modelAnswer: Not ulnar. The low ulnar and MAC sensory responses mean the lesion's past the root ganglion, so it's plexus, not root. Denervation across ulnar and median C8-T1 muscles with normal paraspinals says lower trunk.

parts.label: What I do
parts.criteria: Calls the provider the same day with the localization and the Horner syndrome in a smoker with weight loss, recommending urgent chest imaging.
parts.modelAnswer: Call his provider today: lower trunk plexopathy with Horner in a heavy smoker who's losing weight. He needs chest imaging now.

missed.headline: Apical tumor missed
missed.body: SNAPs tell you where the lesion is: low SNAPs mean a lesion beyond the root ganglion. A low MAC SNAP with C8-T1 denervation and Horner syndrome is a lower trunk plexopathy; in a smoker, image the lung apex.

safe.headline: Localized and flagged
safe.body: You used the SNAPs to localize past the ulnar nerve to the lower trunk, linked the Horner syndrome and called within minutes. That is the expert path.

scoring.modelReasoning: SNAP amplitude reflects the number of sensory axons; because the sensory cell body sits in the dorsal root ganglion, a root lesion spares the SNAP and a plexus or nerve lesion lowers it. CMAP amplitude reflects motor axons, muscle and the neuromuscular junction together. Mr. Hale has low ulnar and medial antebrachial cutaneous SNAPs, C8-T1 denervation across ulnar and median muscles and normal paraspinals: a lower trunk plexopathy. With Horner syndrome, shoulder pain, weight loss and heavy smoking, an apical (Pancoast) tumor must be imaged.
